Jonathan Castro, lettering for a Skechers China project

Four lines of spiky chrome lettering on black, each wrapped in a different neon glow, for a Skechers project in China.

Source
AIGA Eye on Design (5 September 2019): “Acid Graphics” Are the New Psychedelia
Creator
Jonathan Castro
Made
Before September 2019 (the article does not give a year)
Style
Acid graphics (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Aggressive, futuristic, synthetic, loud
Evidence
Inspected the 1200 px image Jonathan-Castro-skechers-china-jonathan-castro-.jpg that Eye on Design published with the article, in a scratch folder. Not stored. 2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Eye on Design shows this image in its 2019 article on acid graphics, with the caption “Jonathan Castro. Skechers China project”. The article does not say what the project was or when it ran.

Observed

  • Four lines of lettering are centred on a pure black ground: “2028” (or similar) with Chinese characters, “SKECHERS”, “MOVE”, and a long wide word that is hard to read.
  • The letters are rendered as polished, bevelled chrome with gray-to-white reflections and dark bands.
  • Thorny spurs and blade-like points grow from the letterforms. Some lines are drawn in hairline outlines, others as solid chrome.
  • Each line has a different glow or outline: acid yellow-green, hot pink, cyan, or electric blue. Acid yellow-green also fills streaks inside the chrome.
  • Lines overlap each other, and legibility is low.

Why it belongs

The work shows the style at its most concentrated: chrome as the material of the letters, spiky custom letterforms, and neon accents on black. It is close to Y2K in its chrome, but its sharp spurs and aggressive tone separate it.

Borrow

Grow thorny spurs from a few stroke ends of a wide display face, and render the letters as chrome.

Give each display line its own single accent glow on a black ground.
